Travel Advisory Level 3 : Reconsider Travel Travel Advisory Level 3: Reconsider travelto Saudi Arabia due to risk of drone and missile targeting of American interests by Iran and the Iranian-supported Houthis, armed conflict, terrorism, exit bans, and local laws regarding social media activity. Some areas have increased risk. Read the entire Travel Advisory. Read More... Worldwide Caution The Department of State advises Americans worldwide to exercise increased caution. Consular Information for Americans in the Middle East Americans in the Middle East should follow the latest guidance from the nearest U.S. embassy or consulate. Enroll in STEP to receive the latest security updates. Americans who need assistance: call 24/7 at +1-202-501-4444 (from abroad) and +1-888-407-4747 (from the U.S. and Canada) Alerts for U.S. Citizens Read alerts for U.S. Citizens Emergency Assistance Local Emergency Information and Contacts Visit Travel.State.gov for More Information Close ⨉ Help us improve Security Alert: U.S. Mission to Saudi Arabia – October 25, 2026 By U.S. Mission Saudi Arabia 12 MINUTE READ October 25, 2026 Effective October 23, 2026, the Department of State ordered non-emergency U.S. government employees and U.S. government employee family members to leave Saudi Arabia due to safety risks. Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area. U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia require special authorization from Chief of Mission to use any airport in Saudi Arabia following recent missile and UAV attacks on airports in the Kingdom. King Khalid International Airport (RUH) in Riyadh announced a partial reopening as of October 25 for domestic flights and some international flights operated by national carriers. A limited number of flights normally based at RUH are operating out of Qassim-based Prince Naif bin Abdulaziz International Airport (ELQ). Operations at King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah (JED) are operational with some delays and cancellations. Operations at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam (DMM) are operational with some delays and cancellations. U.S. citizens should be aware of potential attacks on airports, airspace closures, flight cancellations, and travel disruptions.  Please take extreme caution if you choose to use airports in Saudi Arabia.  We recommend checking your flight departure status directly with the airline and with the airport. Private car, train, and bus options may provide alternatives to air travel to or from Saudi Arabia.  Below are some transportation resources for your consideration.  Please confirm availability and schedules directly with the providers. Saudi Arabia Railways: https://www.sar.com.sa/ SAT Transportation: https://satrans.com.sa/ SAPTCO: https://saptco.com.sa/en All land border crossings, including the King Fahd Causeway to Bahrain, remain operational.   All highways and roads in and around Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dhahran remain operational. International airports in neighboring countries of Bahrain (BAH), Jordan (AMM), Oman (MCT), Qatar (DOH), and the United Arab Emirates (AUH, DXB, SHJ) remain operational.  Please confirm status directly with airports. Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Interior continues to warn that “filming, publishing, or sharing information related to counter missiles and drones, and their impact sites, exposes you to legal liability.”  U.S. citizens have been detained for not adhering to these regulations, including taking photos of government buildings, airports, and impact sites.  Visitors and residents are subject to local laws while in Saudi Arabia. U.S. citizens are reminded to follow the guidance of national alerts released by Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defense via cellular broadcast. U.S. Government Employee Travel Restrictions: U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia require special authorization from Chief of Mission to use any airport in Saudi Arabia.  U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia are not allowed to travel within 20 miles of the Yemen border due to safety risks and need special authorization for travel to the provinces of Jizan, Asir, Najran, and the cities of Qatif, Yanbu, and Taif. Operational Status: Emergency consular services are available for U.S. citizens. Actions to Take: Review the State Department’s Travel Advisory for Saudi Arabia . Review the State Department’s Travel Advisory for Yemen . Enroll in the Department of State’s  Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) .  STEP enrollment gives you the latest security updates and makes it easier for the U.S. embassy or consulate to contact you in an emergency. If an aerial attack occurs, stay away from glass doors, windows, and any fallen debris, and monitor your phone and news outlets for official guidance. Keep your cell phone charged and pre-programmed with emergency numbers, including those below for the embassy and consulates. Be aware of your surroundings. Avoid all demonstrations and large gatherings. Avoid all areas where there is a heavy police presence. Monitor local media. Follow the instructions of local authorities. Contact your airline directly for flight change details if your flight is affected. Exercise caution and stay alert at locations publicly associated with the United States. Keep a low profile. Assistance: Local Emergency Information Unified Emergency (police, firefighters, and others): 911 Police: 999 Ambulance: 997 Highway Security: 996 Medical Assistance For medical emergencies in Saudi Arabia, the Sulaiman Al Habib Hospital system provides English-language medical care in all major cities.  For Riyadh specifically, additional medical facilities include the Soliman Fakeeh Hospital and the Specialized Medical Center (SMC), which has two branches in the capital.  For Jeddah specifically, additional medical facilities include the Dr. Soliman Fakeeh Hospital and the International Medical Center Hospital.
